name: Unicode TAG-block (U+E0000-U+E007F) smuggled into a tool description
notes: ASCII smuggling: the description carries 'ignore previous instructions' encoded entirely in the Unicode TAG block, which renders as nothing in an approval UI but is recoverable by a model that decodes tag codepoints. Method from arXiv 2607.05744 (2026-07-07), which reported TAG-block concealment defeating string-matching sanitizers. mcpm already blocks this class: HIDDEN_CHAR_CLASS covers U+E0000-U+E007F, so H2 flags the presence on block-capable metadata targets. This fixture is the proof. Note the injection signature does NOT also fire here — PATTERN_BREAKERS strips TAG chars before matching, so a fully TAG-encoded phrase collapses to nothing; presence detection is what catches it.
